observations: The page number «97» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. At the foot, the signature line of the printed sheet: «D. K. D. Vidensk. Selsk. Skr., 7. Række, hist. og filos. Afd. III. 1.» on the left and the sheet number «13» on the right; recorded here, not transcribed as a line. L01 continues the sentence that ends p. 96 (JP2 0128, L37), «Die sechs grössten Kreise gehen».

L15: the formula in the line, inside tall parentheses, its fractions built up in smaller type, written {cf:NUMERATOR|DENOMINATOR}; the minus signs long dashes (37 px in the numerator, 47 px in the line) with a space on either side. L07: «59—59b», the long dash set close, the b raised. L09: «Naẓīr», in italics, with the dot under the z and the macron.

L01-L19. Checked: the ascendant lies on the horizon, so that its right ascension is that of the midheaven plus its half day arc, and adding its half night arc gives the right ascension of the midheaven plus 180°, the lower midheaven, the beginning of the IV. house; adding then the half day arc gives the right ascension of the ascendant plus 180°, that of the opposite point of the ecliptic, the beginning of the VII. house, as L17-L19 say. The day arc and the night arc make 360°, so that a sixth of the day arc is 60° less a sixth of the night arc, as in L15.

L20-L25. Checked: the houses I-III and VII-IX each take a sixth of the night arc of the ascendant in right ascension, IV-VI and X-XII a sixth of its day arc. The two arcs are equal when the ascensional difference vanishes, tan φ · tan δ = 0, φ the latitude and δ the declination of the degree of the ascendant: at the equator always, at other latitudes when the ascendant is one of the equinoctial points. The size of the houses therefore follows the degree that rises, which changes in the course of every day; the season, in L24-L25 and N03, governs it when the ascendant is the place of the sun, as at sunrise.

L26-L36 and N04-N06. Checked: with al-Battānī's obliquity 23° 35′ the declination of 297° 3′ is 20° 52′ south; at the latitude 38° 30′ of N04 the ascensional difference is 17° 40′, the day arc 144° 41′ and its twelfth 12° 3′, «12° 4′» (with the latitude 37° 53′ of Cordova 12° 7′). Al-Battānī's table of the seasonal hours (Nallino II, 67) gives for Ḥarrān (36° 40′) 12° 3′ at 20° and 12° 20′ at 30° of Capricorn, 12° 15′ for 27° 3′, the value of the same computation at 36° 40′. 2 × 12° 4′ = 24° 8′; 2 × (30° − 12° 4′) = 35° 52′.

L12: «III. bezw. IX.)»; see the critical note. L27: «man» at the end of the line, the right side of its n faint; read as «man». L36: «ist also = 35° 52′», as Suter writes «ist also bei dieser Anomalie = 52′ 47″ — 12′ 20″» (p. 90, JP2 0122, L28).
Small specks before «Man» (L20), in the left margin beside L22 and after «einer» (L26); not transcribed.
